RENDERING PIPELINE (implement each stage explicitly, with code comments):
1. Geometry: cube with 8 vertices (±1,±1,±1); 6 quad faces each split into exactly 2 triangles (12 triangles total); each face gets a distinct base RGB color (nice palette). Vertex normals = normalized average of the 3 adjacent face normals, i.e. (±1,±1,±1)/√3, so light interpolates smoothly across faces (real Gouraud gradients, not flat shading).
2. Rotation matrices: each frame build a combined 3×3 matrix R = Rz·Ry·Rx from three time-accumulated angles with different per-axis speeds (e.g. 0.7, 1.0, 0.45 rad/s); transform vertex positions AND vertex normals by R (rotation is orthonormal so normals use the same matrix).
3. Moving light source: a point light orbiting the cube (radius ≈ 3.2 around Y, with vertical bobbing on a different frequency). Per-vertex Lambert lighting: L = normalize(lightPos − worldPos); diffuse = max(0, N·L); vertexColor = faceColor × (ambient ≈ 0.18 + diffuse × intensity), clamped 0–255.
4. Perspective projection: camera at origin looking down +z; viewZ = worldZ + 4; sx = cx + x·f/viewZ, sy = cy − y·f/viewZ, focal length f chosen so the cube fills roughly 60–70% of screen height.
5. Backface culling: per-triangle view-space normal = cross(edge1, edge2); cull triangle if dot(normal, triangle centroid in view space) ≥ 0 (camera at origin). 
6. Depth handling: painter's algorithm — sort surviving triangles by average viewZ, far→near.
7. Software rasterizer (Gouraud): for each triangle compute bounding box clamped to canvas, then per-pixel barycentric edge functions (use incremental edge-function stepping for speed, pixel centers at +0.5); interpolate R,G,B affinely across the triangle; write into a Uint32Array view of an ImageData framebuffer as 0xFF000000 | (b<<16) | (g<<8) | r with one-time endianness detection; blit once per frame with putImageData. Skip degenerate triangles (zero signed area).
8. Clear: fill the framebuffer with near-black (e.g. #0b0d12) at the start of every frame.

FEATURES:
- Key W toggles wireframe mode: when ON, skip filled rasterization and instead stroke the edges of every visible (culling-passing) triangle via Canvas 2D paths, stroke color = face base color modulated by the triangle's average vertex light intensity, lineWidth ≈ 1.5, round joins. Backface culling still applies in wireframe mode.
- Key P toggles pause: freezes cube rotation AND light motion, but the render loop, FPS measurement, and W toggle keep working; show a clear "PAUSED" indicator.
- FPS display: exponential moving average of frame deltas from performance.now(), shown every frame in a corner monospace HUD together with frame time in ms, triangles drawn count, current mode (shaded/wireframe), and control hints "W — wireframe" / "P — pause". HUD text drawn after putImageData so it stays crisp.
- Visualize the moving light: after putImageData, project the light position to screen and draw a soft radial-gradient glow (warm white/yellow core, transparent falloff) so the orbiting light is visible in both modes.
- requestAnimationFrame main loop; clamp dt to 50 ms; accumulate rotation angles from dt so pause/resume works correctly.
- Handle window resize: recreate canvas size, ImageData, framebuffer, focal length. Render at CSS pixel resolution (devicePixelRatio capped to 1) for performance.
